Each contact missing a full name or an age is looked up on CyberBackgroundChecks, a people-search site, in the app\'s browser, using the name, number or email you have for them. It can take a minute or more per contact, and you may be asked to solve CAPTCHAs. Everyone is looked up first; then you choose, contact by contact, which person found is yours. You can stop at any time and choose from what was found so far.

The app reads the people saved on your phone, and can import friends from other accounts if you ask it to.

Once a day, when your phone is online and its battery isn\'t low, each contact\'s name is looked up in public jail, prison, court and obituary records, and in the news. You\'re told if something turns up.

Many people share a name. A record that resembles someone you know is often someone else. The app shows you why it thinks a record fits, and no death or arrest is recorded about a contact until you confirm it.
You may learn that someone has died or been arrested. Alerts about either can be turned off in Settings; matches still wait for you in the app.

Your contact list stays on your phone. To check someone, their name is sent to the records and news sites being searched; looking up missing details sends their name, number or email to a people-search site. Each checked contact\'s note gets a short line from the app: that they\'re checked daily, or a status you confirmed. Notes sync with your contacts account; a possible match is never written there. A setting turns the notes off.
